description: Per-skill evaluation for plugin-ecosystem-architect — validates trigger routing, boundary discipline against library-linkage-architect / api-designer / developer-relations-advocate, and the ground rules R1-R6 the skill exists to enforce.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a plugin-platform design request
scenarios.input: We want third-party developers to build extensions for our product. Where do we start?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for a capability-model question
scenarios.input: How should extensions declare what they are allowed to access in our app?

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when extensions keep breaking
scenarios.input: Every time we release, half our third-party integrations break. How do we fix that?

scenarios.description: The binary ABI shape belongs to library-linkage-architect
scenarios.input: Should our plugin boundary use a C ABI or pass C++ objects across it?

scenarios.description: Network API versioning belongs to api-designer
scenarios.input: How should we version our public REST API for v2 so existing clients keep working?

scenarios.description: Building one integration belongs to automation-engineer
scenarios.input: Build us a Zapier-style integration that syncs our tickets to the customer's Slack.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse to retrofit an extension boundary after the core ships (R1)
scenarios.input: We've shipped v1 of the product. Now let's bolt on a plugin system so partners can extend it.

patterns: just bolt on a plugin system

scenarios.description: Agent must require stability tiers and version negotiation (R2)
scenarios.input: We'll just try not to break the plugin API. Do we need to formalize anything?
Our plugin manifest lists permissions like 'network' and 'files', and the docs say plugins shouldn't abuse them.

scenarios.description: Agent must require a removal/revocation path (R4)
scenarios.input: Plugins can be installed from our store. If one turns out to be malicious we'll just handle it then.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse in-process untrusted code without isolation (R5)
scenarios.input: Plugins will run in-process with full access to our app's memory. It's much faster that way.

scenarios.description: Agent must require a DX deliverable (R6)
scenarios.input: We'll publish the plugin API docs. Developers should be able to figure out the rest.

scenarios.description: A full platform request should surface capabilities, contract, lifecycle and DX
scenarios.input: Design our complete extension platform, end to end.

scenarios.description: Agent should flag silent capability expansion on update
scenarios.input: When we push a plugin update that needs a new permission, we just grant it automatically to avoid interrupting users.

scenarios.description: Output should be specific and actionable rather than hedged
scenarios.input: What is the most important thing to know about building a plugin platform?
